name: Exit Code Lookup
description: Look up what Linux and Unix command exit codes mean.

hints.query: Accepts an exit code (127) or a keyword; typing filters locally, there is nothing to run.
hints.output: Every exit code is listed by default; typing a search term or picking a category narrows the list instantly, row by row as "code / meaning / category / explanation".

faq.q: Why does 137 show up so often in containers?
faq.a: 137 = 128 + 9 means the process was killed by SIGKILL, most often because the OOM killer ran out of memory.
Not always. A zero exit only means the command considered itself successful; errors inside a script may never be checked.

faq.q: What is the difference between 126 and 127?
faq.a: 126 means the command was found but could not be executed, usually a permission problem; 127 means the command does not exist or is not on PATH.
